correctness.rationale: Direct edge-distance signatures on the 21 Fano incidence flags give a necessary and sufficient 210-pair separating test. Exhaustive enumeration of every <=5 landmark subset yields none below 5 and 168 at 5. Independent incidence-geometric code proves exactly 84 point-triangle/tangent configurations and 84 dual configurations with no other five-set bases. Full replacement enumeration proves jump degree 5, 420 edges, diameter 5, and slide decomposition 21 C8, with union-of-state supports equal to all 21 original eight-cycle supports. Both programs passed and are included with exact outputs.

value.rationale: The Fano point-line incidence graph is a canonical distance-transitive cubic cage; identifying all optimal vertex landmarks for its 21 edges is a natural sensing/code question. The classification exposes two 84-member geometric families and a sharp reconfiguration distinction: globally connected 5-regular jumping versus 21 isolated 8-cycle slide components, with each component corresponding to an actual eight-cycle of the original graph. This answers a motivated optimum-space structure question, not just an isolated scalar invariant.
